prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the camera wearer moving from a dimly lit adjacent room (frame 1, with a table ~1.5–3 m on the left and a wall ~1–1.5 m on the right) into a narrow galley kitchen (frames 2–3) and turning right to face a stove and counter (frames 4–5). In frames 2 and 3, the left wall and upper cabinets are very bright (~0.5–1.5 m away, within arm's reach in frame 3), the sink counter stretches from ~1 m to ~2.5 m ahead on the left, the refrigerator stands on the right (~1.5–2.5 m away), and a dark doorway at the far end recedes beyond 4–5 m. In frames 4 and 5, as the wearer turns right and approaches the stove, the foreground cooking pot with handle, stove surface, small bowl, and range hood above appear bright at ~0.4–0.8 m (well within arm's reach), with a kettle and utensil holders slightly further back (~0.8–1.2 m) and the refrigerator directly to the left of the counter. Compared to the dark and motion-blurred RGB frames (especially frame 1 and the blurred kitchen transition in frame 3), the depth map clearly reveals the continuous 3D geometry of the table, walls, sink basins, and individual vessels on the stove. However, it is unreliable in the distant doorway where the person visible in RGB (frames 2–3, ~4–5 m away) is completely lost in uniform black depth, and along the lower-left edge of frame 5 where the nearby floor/cabinet drops out to black.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies key kitchen appliances and vessels across frames 2–5, showing the sink on the left (~1–2 m away) and the refrigerator and distant person on the right in frame 2, shifting to the refrigerator on the left (~0.8–1.5 m away) and the oven/stove with bowls, a bottle, and a spoon in front (~0.4–1.0 m away, within arm's reach) in frames 4 and 5. In frame 2, it segments a partially occluded person standing sideways/angled in the distant doorway (~4–5 m ahead, just left of the refrigerator mask), which helps confirm the presence of a person that is tiny and easy to miss in the RGB strip. As the wearer moves forward and turns right from frame 2 to frame 5, the refrigerator mask shifts from the right edge of the view to the left edge, while the stove, cooking pan (labelled 'bowl'), and utensils grow larger in the lower-right foreground. However, the map is completely blank in frame 1 and exhibits major reliability issues in frames 3–5: in frame 3, a massive false 'oven' mask covers the backsplash, counter, and hallway while the sink is split into overlapping duplicate masks and the distant person is missed. In frames 4 and 5, the stove is inconsistently segmented (merging with the counter or refrigerator edge), the skillet and kettle are misclassified as 'bowl', and a metal canister above the stove is misclassified as a 'bottle'.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, detecting neither body skeletons nor hand keypoints anywhere in the sequence. Based on the RGB context, no hands or body parts of the camera wearer are visible within the field of view, even when the wearer stands within arm's reach (~0.4–0.8 m) of the sink counter in frame 3 and the stove top in frames 4 and 5. The only other person in the scene appears in the distant hallway through the doorway in frames 2 and 3 (~4–5 m away in front of the wearer), standing upright and facing roughly leftward/sideways across the doorway without looking toward the camera wearer. Because this distant person is heavily occluded by the doorframe in frame 2 and severely motion-blurred in frame 3, the pose estimator fails to register any yellow body or magenta hand skeletons. Consequently, the pose map provides no additional spatial information beyond confirming the absence of close-range visible limbs, and it is unreliable for tracking distant, motion-blurred, or partially occluded figures.
